title: New Zealand created four Maori electorates in 1867
body: New Zealand's 1867 law created four parliamentary electorates for Maori representation. Later rules allowed their number to change based on the census and how many voters of Maori descent chose the Maori electoral roll.
takeaway: Representation can use overlapping maps for voters enrolled in different ways.
source: New Zealand Electoral Commission, Maori Electoral Option Media Kit (2023)

title: The House of Lords can delay certain money bills by only a month
body: Under the UK's Parliament Act 1911, the Speaker can certify a bill as a money bill. If the House of Lords fails to pass it unamended within a month, it can generally proceed to royal assent without the Lords' agreement.
takeaway: A two-chamber parliament can give the chambers different powers over public money.
source: UK House of Commons Library, The Parliament Acts
visual: a closed document folder on the red benches of a parliamentary chamber

title: Queen Anne refused royal assent to a bill in 1708
body: The Scottish Militia Bill passed both Houses of the British Parliament, but Queen Anne withheld royal assent in 1708. The UK National Archives identifies it as the last time a monarch refused assent to a bill that passed both houses.
takeaway: A power can persist in the formal procedure long after the last time it was used to block a bill.
source: UK National Archives, Original Acts of Parliament and Royal Assent
